_comment: AINOS3-100 AC8 — per-technique expected footprint: which telemetry field must move, and how.
⚠ ANCHORED ON WHAT EACH SCRIPT COMMANDS, not on what the corpus happens to show.
Deriving the expected footprint from the same data it validates is circular, and a
generic novel-value check cannot substitute: measured 2026-09-19, the three probe-only
techniques scored 39/45/49 novel columns, squarely inside the range of real attacks,
because free-running fields (GPS position, scheduler counters) generate novel values
continuously. Each entry below names the command that produces it.
direction: increase | reset | change   (reset = a counter zeroed, i.e. it goes DOWN)
any_of: the footprint holds if ANY listed field moves as specified — used where the
script sends several commands and the corpus need only evidence one.
modes:  restricts the assertion to those ADCS modes. EX-0012.08 commands a mode change,
which is invisible in the run whose hold mode IS the target mode.
⚠ SAMPLING-RATE BLIND SPOT, measured 2026-09-22. Several techniques send a command and
then RESET the counter within the same second (DE-0003.01 does NOOP+RESET in 0.7 s), while
the owning HK packet updates every ~4 s. The counter returns to its old value before it is
ever sampled, so its net observable change is ZERO — CFE_ES.CommandCounter is flat 0 across
all 2,804 frames of a DE-0003.01 run. That is the technique SUCCEEDING (its whole premise is
hiding the command), not a failed attack. For those, the durable evidence is the EVS event
the command generates: CFE_EVS_HK.MessageSendCounter steps at the attack frame (193->197).
⚠ CI.usCmdCnt and TO.usCmdCnt are near-dead (1 change in 2,610 frames) — do not assert on
them; see AINOS3-72 on the lab-vs-full app re-point.
⚠ A RESET is evidence, and an 'increase' test will never see it. DE-0003.08 zeroes the EVS
counter: CFE_EVS_HK.MessageSendCounter goes 192 -> 0 -> 2,3,4,5… The window max NEVER
exceeds the baseline max, because destroying that history IS the technique. Assert
direction 'reset' (a monotonic counter stepping backwards), not 'increase'.
⚠ THE GATE HAS A KNOWN FLOOR, and it is a sampling limit, not a detection limit.
A command whose effect is transient can complete BETWEEN two HK samples and leave no
cadence: in SUNSAFE the counter moves at frames 882 and 930 (0->1->0), in INERTIAL it is
So a footprint MISS means 'not corroborated in telemetry', NOT 'the attack did not run' —
check the EVS event and the subprocess exit before rejecting a run on this gate alone.
⚠ RESOLVED 2026-09-24 (supersedes the 2026-09-23 'MECHANISM UNKNOWN' and the
earlier 'coin flip refuted' notes). A live reproduction with CFE_EVS.Message
temporarily un-excluded settled it: the FSW behaves IDENTICALLY in every mode.
The LOAD of the unstaged /cf/attacker_rts.tbl is rejected ('Unable to open file
... Status = -1'), the ACTIVATE is rejected ('Cannot activate table
'SC.RTS_TBL001'. No Inactive image available'), and CFE_TBL.CommandCounter goes
0->1 while CommandErrorCounter goes 0->2 -- in INERTIAL exactly as in the other
modes. There is NO INERTIAL-specific rejection.
The miss is the collection LEVEL: these three were collected at level 4, whose
cleanup(reset_counters=True) zeroes those counters ~2.8 s after ACTIVATE. That
observable window is shorter than the ~4 s CFE_TBL HK cadence, so ~30 % of runs
in ANY mode never sample the excursion. EX-0012.04/INERTIAL going 2/2 was
small-sample bad luck -- a 3rd INERTIAL instance caught it 0->1/0->2 -- and the
earlier '2/2 while siblings go 8/8' reasoning under-weighted how a ~30 % miss
distributes over n=2.
FIX: build_corpus_batch.restore_levels now treats cleanup(reset_counters=True)
as a restore, so .03/.04/.05 collect at LEVEL 3 (LOAD+ACTIVATE, no reset). The
counters then stay elevated for the rest of the run and are always sampled. The
CFE_TBL.Command*Counter fields below are therefore both robust AND attack-
specific at level 3; no EVS-counter fallback is added, because
CFE_EVS_HK.MessageSendCounter climbs continuously from background EVS traffic
(RADIO/ADCS events) and would make the gate pass even for a run that never fired.

DE-0003.01.note: counter is reset faster than its ~4 s HK cadence, so the EVS event is the observable evidence
